hints.title: Invert to Days Array
hints.text: Create an array days where days[x] is the day on which bulb x turns on. The problem now asks for two positions left and right with right minus left equals k plus one.

hints.title: Intermediate Bulb Constraint
hints.text: For bulb positions left and right to bloom with k empty slots between them, every position i between left and right must bloom after both left and right.

hints.title: Sliding Window Invariant
hints.text: Scan indices with left at position 1 and right at position 1 plus k plus one. If an intermediate index blooms earlier than left or right, advance left to that index and reset right.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def kEmptySlots(self, bulbs: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(bulbs)
        days = [0] * (n + 1)
        for day, pos in enumerate(bulbs, 1):
            days[pos] = day

        ans = float("inf")
        left, right = 1, k + 2
        i = 1
        while right <= n:
            if i < right:
                if days[i] < days[left] or days[i] < days[right]:
                    left = i
                    right = i + k + 1
                i += 1
            else:
                ans = min(ans, max(days[left], days[right]))
                left = right
                right = left + k + 1
                i = left + 1

        return ans if ans != float("inf") else -1
```

complexity.notes: Inverted day-position array with sliding window boundary verification.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Maintaining active bulbs in a balanced BST per day costs O(N log N) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Inverting positions into days allows linear scan validation in O(N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Invert the mapping so bulbs become array indices and blooming times become values.
